user: How can one upgrade to a new version using the IBM Cloud CLI and restore from backup?
assistant: To upgrade to a new version and restore from backup using the IBM Cloud CLI,  clicking Restore on a backup brings up a dialog box where you can change some options for the new deployment. One of them is the database version, which is auto-populated with the versions available for you to upgrade to. Select a version and click Restore to start the provision and restore process.  Here's an example for upgrading and restoring a MySQL database:
```bash
ibmcloud resource service-instance-create example-upgrade databases-for-mysql standard us-south -p '{"backup_id": "crn:v1:bluemix:public:databases-for-mysql:us-south:a/54e8ffe85dcedf470db5b5ee6ac4a8d8:1b8f53db-fc2d-4e24-8470-f82b15c71717:backup:06392e97-df90-46d8-98e8-cb67e9e0a8e6", "version":8}'
[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
Requirements for upgrading to MySQL version 8
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
Before upgrading to MySQL version 8, you should follow these requirements:
1. Check for an upgrade with Upgrade Checker Utility in MySQL Shell to check if an upgrade is required for MySQL.
2. Before attempting any upgrades, refer to MySQL's Preparing Your Installation for Upgrade. to ensure upgrade readiness.
3. Change the authentication plugin: In MySQL 8.0, caching_sha2_password is the default authentication plugin rather than mysql_native_password. If you encounter the error 'sha256_password is deprecated and will be removed in a future release', you need to ALTER affected Users to use 'caching_sha2_password'.
For more information about the upgrade process, you can refer to the IBM Cloud Databases documentation on migrating to Databases for MySQL.
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
For upgrading to MySQL version 8, the documents identify checking upgrade compatibility with the **Upgrade Checker Utility in MySQL Shell**. It helps determine whether your current version is compatible with an upgrade package. [S8]

Run the checker from the command line using `mysqlsh`. The documented example checks a MySQL server for upgrade to release **8.0.27** and returns JSON output: [S9]

```bash
mysqlsh -- util checkForServerUpgrade user@localhost:3306
```

To perform the upgrade, restore a backup of your data into a **new deployment running the new database version**. [S5]

The provided excerpts do not establish a complete list of prerequisites for upgrading to MySQL 8.
[The End of Assistant's Answer]

[The Start of Document]
* API







 Upgrading to a new Major Version 

Once a major version of a database is at its End Of Life (EOL), upgrade to a current major version.

Find the available versions of MySQL on the [IBM Cloud® Databases for MySQL catalog](https://cloud.ibm.com/databases/databases-for-mysql/create) page, from the Cloud Databases CLI plug-in command [ibmcloud cdb deployables-show](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-cli-plugin?topic=databases-cli-plugin-cdb-referencedeployables-show), or from the Cloud Databases API [/deployables](https://cloud.ibm.com/apidocs/cloud-databases-apiget-all-deployable-databases) endpoint.

For more information, see [SHA-256 Pluggable Authentication](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sha256-pluggable-authentication.html).

 Back up and Restore Upgrade 

To upgrade your database, initiate the process by [restoring a backup](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mysql?topic=databases-for-mysql-dashboard-backups&interface=clirestore-backup-cli) of your data into a new deployment that is running the new database version.

 Upgrading in the UI 

You can upgrade to a new version when [restoring a backup](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mysql?topic=databases-for-mysql-dashboard-backups&interface=clirestore-backup-cli) from the Backups menu of your Deployment dashboard.

 Check for an upgrade with Upgrade Checker Utility 

The [Upgrade Checker Utility in MySQL Shell](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/mysql-shell/8.0/en/mysql-shell-utilities-upgrade.html) allows you to check if an upgrade is required for MySQL. This function is useful when you want to determine whether your current version is compatible with an upgrade package.

Start the upgrade checker utility from the command line using the [mysqlsh](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/mysql-shell/8.0/en/mysqlsh.html) command interface. The following example checks a MySQL server for upgrade to release 8.0.27, and returns JSON output:

mysqlsh -- util checkForServerUpgrade user@localhost:3306
